review_notes: I read the whole supplied file (lines 1–305). It has no @[simp] declarations, no simp sets, no simp-normal-form definitions, and no local simp attributes. It contains only Harnack-style lemmas about harmonic functions on the unit disc: `continuousOn_u_exp`, `non_neg_boundary`, the normalized upper and lower bounds, `harnack_ineq_cont`, `harmonic_scaling`, `harnack_ineq_aux` and `harnack_ineq`. These are inequality statements, not rewrite rules. Their left-hand sides are not reusable rewrite patterns, so I found no missing canonical simp lemma, no wrong-direction rewrite, no competing rules and no credible rewrite cycle. Inside the proofs, `simp`, `simp_all`, `norm_num` and `field_simp` are called only as local tactics. They are somewhat fragile, but that is a proof-style issue and not a simp-interface defect, and I have no concrete evidence that they cause bad expansion. I did not look through Mathlib for duplicate simp coverage, because I found no candidate to compare against. I could not run Lean, so I make no claim about simplifier behaviour that I did not observe.
